questions.q: What does ACR stand for in the NADCA standard?
questions.explanation: ACR defines minimum performance and procedural requirements for HVAC assessment, cleaning, and restoration. The primary NADCA technical standard.

questions.q: What does SMACNA stand for?
choices: Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors' National Association
Standard Methods for Air Cleaning and Nozzle Application
Society for Mechanical Air Cleaning and Noise Abatement
Sheet Metal Applications, Construction, and National Accreditation
questions.explanation: SMACNA publishes duct design, construction, and installation standards. ANSI/SMACNA 006-2006 covers duct cleaning.

questions.q: What does NAIMA stand for?
choices: National Association of Indoor Mold Abatement
National Airflow and Indoor Mechanical Association
questions.explanation: NAIMA publishes AH-122 (cleaning fibrous glass insulated duct systems). Key reference for insulated ductwork.

questions.q: What does ASHRAE stand for?
choices: American Society for Home Air Regulation Engineering
American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers
Association of Sheet Metal, HVAC, Refrigeration and Air Engineers
American Society for HVAC Research and Engineering
questions.explanation: ASHRAE publishes standards on HVAC design, ventilation, and IAQ. ANSI/ASHRAE/ACCA 180-2018 covers HVAC maintenance.

questions.q: What does IICRC stand for?
choices: Institute of Inspection, Cleaning and Restoration Certification
International Indoor Cleaning and Restoration Council
Institute of Indoor Climate Research and Certification
questions.explanation: IICRC S520 is the Standard and Reference Guide for Professional Mold Remediation.

questions.q: What does NFPA stand for?
questions.explanation: NFPA 90A covers Installation of Air-Conditioning and Ventilation Systems, including fire dampers.

questions.q: What does ACCA stand for?
questions.explanation: ACCA is co-publisher of ANSI/ASHRAE/ACCA 180-2018 on planned HVAC maintenance.

questions.q: Which standard recommends maintaining an inventory of HVAC systems and their locations?
questions.explanation: ASHRAE 180 covers planned maintenance including comprehensive system inventory.

questions.q: What is IICRC S520?
choices: Standard and Reference Guide for Professional Mold Remediation
questions.explanation: S520 is the mold remediation standard. Referenced in ASCS Domains III and IV.

questions.q: What is NFPA 90A?
choices: Standard for Installation of Air-Conditioning and Ventilation Systems
questions.explanation: Covers fire safety requirements for HVAC including fire/smoke dampers and duct materials.

questions.q: What is NAIMA AH-122?
choices: Guide for repairing sheet metal ducts
Guide for cleaning fibrous glass insulated air duct systems
Guide for commissioning new HVAC installations
questions.explanation: Published by NAIMA. Key reference for handling internally insulated ductwork during cleaning.

questions.q: ANSI/SMACNA 006-2006 addresses what subject?
questions.explanation: SMACNA 006 is the sheet metal industry's standard for HVAC duct cleaning practices.

questions.q: What is the recommended sequence for cleaning an HVAC system?
questions.explanation: Clean from dirtiest components first. Mnemonic: EARS (Exhaust, Air handler, Return, Supply).

questions.q: According to the ACR standard, properly performed HVAC cleaning should achieve what measurable result?
choices: Visibly clean to the naked eye
Restore the evaporator coil to its original pressure drop
questions.explanation: ACR uses pressure drop restoration as the measurable benchmark, not visual inspection.

questions.q: According to ACR, coil cleaning should be performed on which sides?
choices: Both the upstream AND downstream sides
questions.explanation: Both sides must be cleaned per NADCA standard, not just one.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of an Air Filtration Device (AFD) during duct cleaning?
choices: To protect system components by filtering debris during cleaning
questions.explanation: AFDs capture contaminants dislodged during cleaning, preventing recontamination of cleaned sections.

questions.q: What does 'source removal' mean in the NADCA context?
choices: Physically removing contaminants from the HVAC system
questions.explanation: NADCA was founded on source removal as the only acceptable cleaning method. Chemical treatment alone does not qualify.

questions.q: What is contact vacuuming?
choices: Vacuuming with the nozzle held close but not touching the surface
Vacuuming where the nozzle directly contacts the surface being cleaned
Using a HEPA vacuum in the mechanical room
questions.explanation: Contact vacuuming requires direct nozzle-to-surface contact for effective debris removal.

questions.q: What should happen BEFORE any HVAC cleaning begins?
choices: Turn off the power to the system
A full visual inspection to assess condition and scope
questions.explanation: ACR requires pre-cleaning visual inspection and assessment. Scope of work is defined before any cleaning.

questions.q: What is the purpose of establishing negative air pressure during cleaning?
choices: To pull contaminants toward the AFD and prevent cross-contamination
To clean more efficiently with less equipment
questions.explanation: Negative pressure draws contaminants toward the collection point, keeping cleaned areas clean.

questions.q: When should access openings be cut in ductwork?
choices: As necessary to allow access to all system components, per industry code
Only when specified on mechanical plans
questions.explanation: Access openings are cut as needed, then closed per NFPA/SMACNA requirements (1" holes plugged or 8" patches with screws and mastic).

questions.q: When repairing an 8" access hole in a sheet metal duct, what is required?
choices: A sheet metal patch secured with screws around the perimeter and sealed with mastic
Duct tape over a foil patch
questions.explanation: Screws around perimeter/corners + mastic sealant + insulation restoration on internally insulated ducts.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable method of source removal?
choices: Air washing with compressed air plus vacuum
questions.explanation: Chemical treatment alone is not source removal per NADCA. Physical extraction is required.

questions.q: What's the role of mechanical agitation in duct cleaning?
choices: To loosen contaminants from duct surfaces so they can be captured
questions.explanation: Brushes, air whips, and skipper balls dislodge debris that negative pressure then captures.

questions.q: When cleaning fiberglass-lined ductwork, what cleaning method is LEAST appropriate?
choices: Stiff wire brush with aggressive agitation
questions.explanation: Stiff agitation damages fiberglass liner. NAIMA AH-122 calls for gentle methods on fibrous lining.

questions.q: What does the acronym 'AHU' stand for?
questions.explanation: Air Handling Unit. The central component containing blower, coils, and filter rack.

questions.q: After cleaning, how should filters be treated?
choices: Replaced with new filters of equal or better MERV rating
Left out until the next service
questions.explanation: Pre-cleaning-era filters are contaminated. Replacement is standard practice post-cleaning.

questions.q: What is the NADCA-recommended method for verifying cleaning has been performed adequately?
choices: NADCA Vacuum Test, coil pressure drop, visual inspection
questions.explanation: NADCA Vacuum Test (gravimetric), pressure drop restoration, and visual inspection are the ACR verification methods.

questions.q: When cleaning an evaporator coil, what is the preferred method?
choices: Spray non-acid coil cleaner, allow dwell time, rinse thoroughly
questions.explanation: Foaming non-acid coil cleaner + dwell + rinse is the standard approach. Acid damages aluminum fins.

questions.q: What does 'mastic' refer to in duct cleaning?
choices: A duct sealant applied at joints and patches
questions.explanation: Mastic is the sealant applied around duct joints, access patches, and seams.

questions.q: Pressure washing in duct cleaning is typically used on what components?
choices: Grilles, registers, diffusers, and exterior coil surfaces
questions.explanation: Grilles, registers, diffusers are removed and washed. Coils are washed in place. Interior duct interiors are cleaned dry or with contained wet methods.

questions.q: What is a VAV box?
choices: Vacuum Air Valve, a pressure regulator
Variable Air Volume terminal unit, controls zone airflow
questions.explanation: VAV boxes modulate airflow to different zones. Must be identified and addressed in commercial duct cleaning.

questions.q: When should you reseal ductwork after creating an access opening?
choices: Immediately after the section is cleaned and inspected
At the end of the entire project
Only if the owner requests it
questions.explanation: Seal as you go to prevent contamination of adjacent cleaned sections.

questions.q: A 1-inch inspection hole in rigid duct should typically be closed with what?
choices: A sheet metal plug or rubber grommet approved for HVAC use
questions.explanation: Approved pop plugs or sheet metal patches. Duct tape alone is not code-compliant.

questions.q: In a building with long duct runs, what is the maximum recommended cleaning distance from a single access opening?
questions.explanation: Practical cleaning reach is around 10-12 feet; more access openings are cut as needed for longer runs or turns.

questions.q: What is the purpose of HEPA filtration on the AFD?
choices: To capture sub-micron particles before air is discharged back to the space
questions.explanation: AFDs use HEPA filtration to ensure clean exhaust when vented indoors or to return captured contaminants safely.

questions.q: Coil cleaners that are labeled 'non-acid' are typically what type of chemistry?
questions.explanation: Non-acid coil cleaners are alkaline, safe for aluminum fins but can burn skin. PPE required.

questions.q: What's the primary reason for cleaning the return side before the supply side?
choices: Return side typically carries more contamination inward; cleaning it first prevents recontaminating the supply
questions.explanation: Dirtiest-to-cleanest sequencing within the air handler section.

questions.q: When is it appropriate to apply an antimicrobial to ductwork?
choices: Only after physical cleaning and only with an EPA-registered product labeled for HVAC use
Before cleaning to kill contaminants first
questions.explanation: Antimicrobials supplement but do not replace source removal. Must be EPA-registered for the specific application.

questions.q: Turning vanes in ductwork primarily serve to:
choices: Direct airflow around 90-degree bends and reduce turbulence
questions.explanation: Vanes are installed inside elbows to smooth airflow and reduce pressure loss.

questions.q: What is the preferred approach for cleaning flexible duct?
choices: Same as rigid duct, contact vacuum
Typically replaced rather than cleaned, due to fragile inner liner
questions.explanation: Flex duct inner liners are fragile. If heavily contaminated, replacement is often more cost-effective and code-compliant.

questions.q: What are the primary components of an Air Handling Unit (AHU)?
choices: Blower/fan, coils (heating and/or cooling), filter rack, drain pan
questions.explanation: AHU = fan + coils + filter rack + drain pan + cabinet. Sometimes includes humidifier or economizer.

questions.q: What does 'CFM' measure?
choices: Cubic Feet per Minute — airflow rate
questions.explanation: CFM quantifies how much air passes through a point per minute.

questions.q: What is a 'plenum' in an HVAC system?
choices: The pressurized chamber that collects or distributes air to/from the air handler
questions.explanation: Supply plenum distributes air out; return plenum collects air back to the AHU.

questions.q: What is the function of a fire damper?
choices: Automatically close to prevent fire spread through ductwork penetrating fire-rated barriers
questions.explanation: Fire dampers seal ducts passing through fire-rated walls or floors when heat triggers them.

questions.q: How does a smoke damper differ from a fire damper?
choices: Smoke dampers use water, fire dampers don't
Smoke dampers close on smoke detection to prevent smoke migration; fire dampers close on heat
Smoke dampers only exist in residential systems
questions.explanation: Different triggers, different purposes. Combination fire/smoke dampers exist too.

questions.q: What's the role of the drain pan on a cooling coil?
choices: Collect condensate produced when humid air cools below dew point
questions.explanation: Cool coils condense moisture from the airstream. Drain pan collects it and routes it out.

questions.q: A 'fan coil unit' is typically found in what setting?
choices: Hotel rooms, small commercial zones — a localized air-handling unit served by chilled/hot water
questions.explanation: Fan coil units serve small zones with water-based heating/cooling. Common in hotels and apartments.

questions.q: What does 'PTAC' stand for?
questions.explanation: PTACs are self-contained through-wall units common in hotels and apartments.

questions.q: What is an economizer on an AHU?
choices: A damper system that uses outside air for 'free cooling' when conditions permit
questions.explanation: Economizers bring in outside air when it's cool enough to reduce mechanical cooling load.

questions.q: Static pressure in HVAC is measured in:
questions.explanation: Static pressure is typically measured in inches of water column due to small magnitudes.

questions.q: What's the primary purpose of pipe insulation on chilled water supply lines?
choices: Prevent condensation from forming on cold pipes and maintain cooling capacity
questions.explanation: Cold pipes sweat in humid environments; insulation prevents condensation damage.

questions.q: A mechanical room is considered part of the HVAC system when:
choices: It has two or more air handlers
It serves as an air mixing chamber OR open return plenum
questions.explanation: Open return plenum use, or mechanical room acting as mixing space, integrates the room into the airflow path.

questions.q: To prevent contaminants from entering ventilation via the mechanical room:
choices: Keep it clean and do NOT use it for storage
questions.explanation: Per ASHRAE 62.1, mechanical rooms should not be used for storage and must be kept clean.

questions.q: What is the primary source document for locating a building's HVAC systems?
questions.explanation: M-series drawings show HVAC equipment, ductwork, and controls.

questions.q: What happens in a VAV (Variable Air Volume) system?
choices: Airflow volume to each zone is modulated based on zone demand
questions.explanation: VAV modulates airflow per zone via motorized dampers in terminal boxes.

questions.q: What does MERV stand for?
questions.explanation: MERV rates filter efficiency at capturing different particle sizes, scale 1-20.

questions.q: A HEPA filter has what equivalent MERV rating?
questions.explanation: True HEPA = 99.97% at 0.3 microns, which is MERV 17-20 equivalent.

questions.q: Where would HEPA filters most commonly be installed?
questions.explanation: HEPA is for the highest-cleanliness environments where pathogens or particulates must be excluded.

questions.q: HEPA filters capture particles down to what minimum size at 99.97% efficiency?
questions.explanation: The HEPA specification: 99.97% at 0.3 microns (most penetrating particle size).

questions.q: What does IAQ stand for?
questions.explanation: IAQ refers to the overall quality of air inside buildings relative to occupant health and comfort.

questions.q: What are VOCs?
choices: Volatile Organic Compounds — off-gassed chemicals from materials
questions.explanation: VOCs are carbon-based chemicals that vaporize at room temperature. Sources: paints, solvents, furniture, cleaning products.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a typical biological contaminant found in HVAC systems?
questions.explanation: PM2.5 is a combustion/particulate contaminant, not biological. Others are biological.

questions.q: When investigating suspected mold contamination, the ASCS should:
choices: Coordinate with qualified mold remediation professionals per IICRC S520 if beyond scope
Ignore it if the customer didn't ask
questions.explanation: ASCS scope is cleaning; significant mold may require IICRC-certified remediator under S520.

questions.q: What is the PM2.5 particle size threshold?
questions.explanation: PM2.5 = fine particulate matter 2.5 microns or smaller. Penetrates deep into lungs.

questions.q: What particle size is considered 'inhalable' and likely to reach the lower respiratory tract?
questions.explanation: Particles under 10 microns penetrate the respiratory tract; <2.5 microns reach alveoli.

questions.q: What role do dust mites play in HVAC contamination?
choices: Their fecal matter is a significant indoor allergen
questions.explanation: Dust mite allergen is one of the most common indoor allergy triggers; accumulates in soft furnishings and ducts.

questions.q: A humidifier added to an AHU helps address what IAQ issue?
choices: Dry indoor air in winter — below 30% RH
questions.explanation: Humidifiers add moisture during heating season when outdoor humidity is low.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a pre-cleaning inspection?
choices: Document existing condition, identify scope, and photograph for baseline
Required only if the customer requests
questions.explanation: Pre-cleaning inspection documents baseline for scope definition and liability purposes.

questions.q: Before cleaning begins, the ASCS should inspect what?
choices: The entire accessible HVAC system including AHU, ductwork, terminal devices, and related components
questions.explanation: ACR requires full system inspection to define scope and identify pre-existing damage.

questions.q: An ASCS who completes cleaning for a vacant building is approached by a new tenant asking about system condition. The ASCS should:
choices: Answer only questions pertaining to the work they performed
questions.explanation: Professional scope: discuss only what you actually cleaned and observed, not a general system assessment.

questions.q: An ASCS is asked for their opinion on a well-known competitor. What's the professional response?
choices: Offer detailed praise to seem fair
Decline to answer due to conflict of interest
questions.explanation: Professional ethics: decline. Don't criticize competitors or steer business conflicts.

questions.q: What visual access method is commonly used to inspect ductwork interior?
choices: Borescope, inspection camera, or remote-controlled inspection robot
questions.explanation: Borescopes and robotic cameras allow interior visualization without destructive access.

questions.q: What should the scope of work document?
choices: Components to be cleaned, components excluded, methods, expected outcomes, and customer acknowledgment
questions.explanation: A proper SOW defines inclusions, exclusions, methods, outcomes, and customer sign-off.

questions.q: During inspection, the ASCS finds visible mold growth. What's the appropriate response?
choices: Clean it with bleach and proceed
Document it, inform the customer, and consider whether it's within scope or requires a qualified remediator
questions.explanation: Document, communicate, and respect scope boundaries per IICRC S520 when significant mold is found.

questions.q: Before cutting access openings, the ASCS should verify what?
choices: Location of wiring, plumbing, and structural members behind the duct
questions.explanation: Cutting blind risks hitting utilities or structure. Verify first.

questions.q: A post-cleaning verification inspection should include:
choices: Visual inspection, NADCA Vacuum Test results, and coil pressure drop comparison
questions.explanation: Verification methods per ACR: visual, gravimetric (NADCA Vacuum Test), pressure drop restoration.

questions.q: What should be photographed during a pre-cleaning inspection?
choices: Representative areas of contamination, damaged components, and conditions that might affect scope
Only the outside of the building
questions.explanation: Before/after photography is standard documentation practice.

questions.q: The ASCS's responsibility during inspection is to:
choices: Identify and document conditions relevant to cleaning; defer to qualified parties for items outside scope
Bill for every minute spent looking
questions.explanation: Stay in lane: identify and document, refer repairs or assessments outside your expertise.

questions.q: What is the purpose of communicating findings to the customer before starting work?
choices: Manage expectations, document pre-existing conditions, and avoid disputes
questions.explanation: Transparent upfront communication prevents scope creep, liability issues, and customer dissatisfaction.

questions.q: OSHA's Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL) for respirable crystalline silica is:
questions.explanation: 29 CFR 1910.1053: 50 µg/m³ 8-hour time-weighted average.

questions.q: What PPE is required when working with non-acid coil cleaner (caustic/alkaline)?
choices: Chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection, and appropriate respirator for inhalation hazards
No PPE needed, it's labeled non-acid
questions.explanation: Non-acid caustic coil cleaners cause serious chemical burns. Gloves + eye pro + respirator per SDS.

questions.q: OSHA's standard for Lockout/Tagout is covered under:
questions.explanation: LOTO is 29 CFR 1910.147 — control of hazardous energy.

questions.q: An SDS must be available to workers for:
choices: Every chemical product used on the job
Only products the owner asks about
questions.explanation: Hazard Communication Standard: SDS required for every hazardous chemical on site, accessible to workers.

questions.q: Confined space entry requires:
choices: A permit program with atmospheric testing, attendant, and rescue plan for permit-required spaces
questions.explanation: 29 CFR 1910.146: permit-required confined spaces need atmospheric testing, attendant, and rescue provisions.

questions.q: When should a respirator be worn during duct cleaning?
choices: When exposure to airborne contaminants exceeds safe levels per SDS, OSHA PEL, or task risk assessment
Only if the customer is watching
questions.explanation: Risk-based: wear respirator when conditions or chemicals demand, per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134.

questions.q: A fit-tested, NIOSH-approved N95 is appropriate for:
choices: Protection against all gases and vapors
Protection against non-oil particulates only, up to the filter's rated efficiency
questions.explanation: N95 = Not for oil aerosol, 95% efficient, particulate only. Gases and vapors require cartridges.

questions.q: In an atmosphere with less than 19.5% oxygen, the appropriate respiratory protection is:
questions.explanation: Oxygen-deficient atmospheres require supplied air; filtering respirators do not add oxygen.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical reason for HVAC cleaning?
choices: Restore designed system airflow and efficiency
Increase the unit's total BTU capacity beyond its design rating
questions.explanation: Cleaning restores designed performance, it doesn't exceed the system's rated capacity.

questions.q: Proper HVAC cleaning is most likely to yield what measurable energy benefit?
choices: Reducing blower motor current by restoring designed static pressure
questions.explanation: Cleaner coils and clearer airways reduce load on the blower motor, modest energy savings.

questions.q: According to NADCA, how often should most HVAC systems be inspected for cleaning need?
choices: After each season, or based on visual inspection showing contamination
questions.explanation: NADCA recommends assessment-based cleaning driven by inspection, not strict time intervals.

questions.q: Which of these is a legitimate trigger for HVAC cleaning?
choices: Following water intrusion or moisture damage
Visible mold growth in ductwork or on coils
questions.explanation: All are ACR-recognized triggers for cleaning.

questions.q: Does HVAC cleaning prevent future contamination?
choices: No, maintenance including filter changes and moisture control is needed ongoing
questions.explanation: Cleaning restores a baseline; ongoing filter maintenance and moisture management are needed to stay clean.
